title: RC Racer Mini Sprint
author: Decent_Assist_4811
selftext:
I made a 16-bit-style RC racing game with Claude: Mini Sprint  
  
[https://rcracemap.com/sprint/](https://rcracemap.com/sprint/)  
  
My kids are avid RC racers. In my spare time I’ve built a few apps and tools for them using Claude Code. Then I thought it might be more fun to make an actual game, so I made Mini Sprint, a homage to classic arcade racer Super Sprint.  
  
There are only few games about real RC racing, and most of them are not very realistic as they use a moving camera. The fixed, top-down, full-track view of Super Sprint though fits really well to RC racing I think. it feels much closer to controlling an RC car from the drivers' stand.  
  
So the game includes my kids’ favourite real-world tracks and all the classes raced in their league. They can connect and use the same RC remote they race with.  
  
While my kids love this, the game is far from finished. All the artwork is AI-generated and still rather inconsistent, there’s no audio yet, and plenty of details need more work. So at the moment, I’m wondering where to take it next.  
  
Should I keep it as a fun little game for my kids, or could it be worth to turn it into a complete game? Should it remain free and browser-based, or could something like this work as a proper Steam release?  
  
I’m not a (game) developer by any means, so any feedback would be greatly appreciated.

comments.author: PerspectiveWorking50
comments.body:
Hi, really cool project! How do you connect a real RC transmitter to Mini Sprint?
Are you using a normal RC receiver with a USB adapter (like the VRC USB adapter), or is the transmitter connected directly to the PC?

replies.author: Decent_Assist_4811
replies.body: We're using the NB4 Noble Pro. You can connect it straight via USB. Older models are recognised automatically as a game controller. Newer models need to be changed to USB mode. In game I run a quick calibration (left/right, acellerate/brake) if a controller is detected. This shoudl also work with other modern remotes.

comments.author: tlxxxsracer
comments.body:
Awesome project! Played some this evening. Sound would be great along with setup changes perhaps. Steering is a bit weird. 

Wish more games were made like this. Great graphics too

replies.author: Decent_Assist_4811
replies.body:
Wow, thank you!   
  
I want to add sound, but I want it to be quite close to the original. The count down voice, the start sound, the electric whirring of the cars etc. I have recordings of races but they have too much wind and noise. Any idea for an (AI?) tool to work on this or generate something fitting?

What did you try for steering? A remote, controller, keyboard?

Setup will come. Currently working in a version for Steam though, hope it's worth it :)
